visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. Built from components/site/v3. No mockup in this directory: the place-type class is the city/community type-card landing, not a Tetherow one-off.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Coldwell Banker type-filtered city results. Those surfaces dump the visitor into a search grid. This page is a place-type node: leftover count and median that already back the type card, a living atlas of the parent city with the type stated in the claim, and a photographed list of that type. Unique title, canonical, ItemList when listings exist. Breadcrumb is City then type, no Home.
note: H1 is `{Type} in {Place}` and it is the page's only display-scale line. SITE-89: a thin V3Carousel filmstrip of photographed listings (shadcn-carousel adapted) sits under the claim in the first viewport, then the Atlas wearing an eyebrow (V3Atlas headlineTone='eyebrow'), not a second Amboqia title. One section-0 sourced claim sentence sits under the H1 with its source line — the count, the lowest ask and the highest all come from ONE listing_tile_mv read; the claim names that the map counts city-limits homes separately because leftover address count and boundary marks disagree (Bend ~766 vs ~495). The Atlas section is UNCONDITIONAL: PlaceTypeAtlasSection streams behind a Suspense boundary whose fallback and whose miss branch are both PlaceTypeAtlasStandin. Rows and marks share one hovered key. Unknown type notFound(). Do not collide with app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug].

tasteReview.beats: Zillow Bend single-family search — we win on Atlas 90-day sales-density cells versus Zillow's pin map; we lose the fold, which is still a restated type title plus a photo strip before the map.

defects.finding: H1 'Single-family in Bend' restates the breadcrumb 'Bend / Single-family' as a second display line with no figure in the title; the 766 and the price range are demoted to body copy under a filing-cabinet tab.
The one sentence treats $397,000 to $11,900,000 as the price band; that is the cheapest and dearest ask, a 30x dump that does not say where Bend single-family actually sits.

The fold's inventory is stills with prices on photos; the only hint the rail moves is a clipped next card with no arrow or dots. SITE-89 required this strip in the 375 fold — layout lock wants Atlas immediately under the claim, so the strip and the lock fight.

defects.section: LISTINGS INSIDE THE BEND CITY LIMITS
defects.finding: The claim says ~766 single-family homes for sale (Bend address); the Atlas legend on the same desktop fold reads ~495 for sale and ~264 pending (city limits). Named as two censuses in the claim; still reads as one broken inventory to the judge.

defects.section: LISTINGS INSIDE THE BEND CITY LIMITS
defects.finding: At 375 the first viewport crops the density map with no fewer/more-sales legend, no for-sale count, no House toggle, and no price scrubber — V3Atlas every-caller (SITE-53), not fixed here.
Just listed / Went pending / Sold render as plain sentences with identical dots — V3Atlas every-caller.
